items.title: Persistent queue starts empty after metadata read error
items.body:
### Component(s)
exporter/exporterhelper

### What happened?
I traced `Start()` through `initClient()` to confirm. If storage returns an error while reading `qmv0`, the queue treats it like unusable metadata, resets to an empty state, and `Start()` still returns nil. If a new request is offered before storage recovers, the fresh write index can overwrite an existing queue entry.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Persist a request in a queue.
2. Restart with a storage client that returns an error for `Get("qmv0")`.
3. Observe that `Start()` succeeds and the queue appears empty.
4. Offer a new request; it can overwrite the stored request at index 0.

**What did you expect to see?**
The startup error is returned, the client is closed, and the stored request remains available after storage recovers.

**What did you see instead?**
The queue starts with empty metadata after a storage read error and may overwrite persisted data on a later offer.

### Collector version
main at 821485556

### Environment information
OS: Windows, amd64
Compiler: Go 1.27.1

### Additional context
Tracking PR: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/pull/16230. The PR adds a regression test for this startup failure.

items.title: [exporterhelper] Sending queue can deadlock when blocked offers are canceled
items.body:
### Component(s)

`exporter/exporterhelper`, `exporter/exporterhelper/internal/queuebatch`

### Summary

Exporter sending queues can deadlock when `block_on_overflow: true` and blocked offers are canceled.

On v0.157.0, a persistent metrics queue stopped at 5,995,714 of 6,000,000 items. Queue and sent counters stopped while the health endpoint remained responsive.

The context-aware [`cond`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/4908404e59e544297b989a6961ee918b6f84b606/exporter/exporterhelper/internal/queue/cond.go#L14-L62) tracks waiters separately from a size-one notification channel. While canceled waiters wait to reacquire the mutex and decrement `waiting`, two closely spaced completion signals can fill the channel and block the second signal while it holds the queue mutex. Reads, offers, completions, and `Size` then stop.

The production path is [`persistentQueue.onDone`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/4908404e59e544297b989a6961ee918b6f84b606/exporter/exporterhelper/internal/queue/persistent_queue.go#L393-L425). [`multiDone.OnDone`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/4908404e59e544297b989a6961ee918b6f84b606/exporter/exporterhelper/internal/queuebatch/partition_batcher.go#L320-L325) can produce the closely spaced completions. [#15468](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/pull/15468#issuecomment-4786651716) includes v0.153.0 stack excerpts reporting one completion blocked in `cond.Signal` and the rest of the queue blocked on the same mutex.

The same code remains on `main` at [`0ffbf34b9da4bd1e499f4eb82ab6c6a8b4669081`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/0ffbf34b9da4bd1e499f4eb82ab6c6a8b4669081/exporter/exporterhelper/internal/queue/cond.go#L14-L62).

### Deterministic reproduction

We ran the test below unchanged against v0.157.0 commit `4908404e59e544297b989a6961ee918b6f84b606`. It fails with `Signal blocked while holding the condition lock`.

The lock-attempt barrier proves both waiters selected cancellation before either notification is sent; the test does not rely on sleeps or queue startup order.

<details>
<summary>Runnable cond_test.go</summary>

```go
// Copyright The OpenTelemetry Authors
// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

package queue

import (
	"context"
	"sync"
	"sync/atomic"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

func TestCondSignalDoesNotBlockBehindCanceledWaiters(t *testing.T) {
	locker := &observedLocker{lockAttempts: make(chan struct{}, 2)}
	c := newCond(locker)

	ctx1, cancel1 := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	ctx2, cancel2 := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	waiter1 := startCondWaiter(locker, c, ctx1)
	waiter2 := startCondWaiter(locker, c, ctx2)

	locked := make(chan struct{})
	notify := make(chan struct{})
	notified := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		locker.Lock()
		close(locked)
		<-notify
		c.Signal()
		c.Signal()
		locker.Unlock()
		close(notified)
	}()

	<-locked
	locker.observe.Store(true)
	cancel1()
	cancel2()
	<-locker.lockAttempts
	<-locker.lockAttempts
	locker.observe.Store(false)
	close(notify)

	select {
	case <-notified:
	case <-time.After(time.Second):
		t.Fatal("Signal blocked while holding the condition lock")
	}

	for _, waiter := range []<-chan error{waiter1, waiter2} {
		select {
		case <-waiter:
		case <-time.After(time.Second):
			t.Fatal("condition waiter did not return")
		}
	}
}

type observedLocker struct {
	mu           sync.Mutex
	observe      atomic.Bool
	lockAttempts chan struct{}
}

func (l *observedLocker) Lock() {
	if l.observe.Load() {
		l.lockAttempts <- struct{}{}
	}
	l.mu.Lock()
}

func (l *observedLocker) Unlock() {
	l.mu.Unlock()
}

func startCondWaiter(l sync.Locker, c *cond, ctx context.Context) <-chan error {
	entered := make(chan struct{})
	done := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() {
		l.Lock()
		close(entered)
		done <- c.Wait(ctx)
		l.Unlock()
	}()

	<-entered
	l.Lock()
	l.Unlock()
	return done
}
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Incident configuration</summary>

```yaml
sending_queue:
  enabled: true
  storage: file_storage
  sizer: items
  queue_size: 6000000
  block_on_overflow: true
  num_consumers: 1
  batch:
    flush_timeout: 5s
    min_size: 10000
    max_size: 10000
    sizer: items
```

</details>

### Expected behavior

`Signal` must not block while its caller holds the condition mutex. Cancellation must not stop unrelated queue work.

### Workaround

Setting `block_on_overflow: false` avoids this wait path after restart, but a full queue returns an enqueue failure instead of blocking. Restarting can restore progress but does not prevent recurrence with the vulnerable setting.

### Related but distinct

This matches the `cond.Signal` stack excerpts in #15468 and is distinct from the startup-recovery deadlock in #12532, whose separate capacity check was removed by #13330.

items.title: [exporter/exporterhelper] Persistent queue deletes queued items on shutdown while the destination is unavailable
items.body:
### Component(s)

exporter/exporterhelper

### What happened?

**Describe the bug**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the bug is. -->

The persistent queue has an explicit carve-out so that requests failing
*because of shutdown* are kept on disk and redelivered after restart
(`internal/queue/persistent_queue.go`, `onDone`):

```go
if experr.IsShutdownErr(consumeErr) {
    // The queue is shutting down, don't mark the item as dispatched, so it's
    // picked up again after restart.
    return
}
```

In practice this branch is almost never taken, because the ONLY producer of
`experr.NewShutdownErr` in the codebase is `internal/retry_sender.go` (~line
145), and only in one narrow case: when a retry **backoff wait** is
interrupted by the retry sender's own `stopCh`. Two consequences:

1. **Exporters that do not enable `retry_on_failure` can never produce a
   shutdown error.** On shutdown, the queue-batch shutdown path drains the
   queue ("Shutdown ... will drain the queue and will call the retry (which
   is stopped) that will only try once every request",
   `internal/queuebatch/queue_batch.go`). If the destination is unavailable
   at that moment, every drained request fails once with an ordinary error,
   `onDone` treats it as a final disposition, and
   `itemDispatchingFinish` **deletes it from persistent storage**. The entire
   backlog that the persistent queue accumulated during the outage is
   destroyed by the act of shutting down — the exact scenario a persistent
   queue exists to survive. (The elasticsearch exporter is one such exporter:
   it performs retries inside its bulk indexer rather than via
   `retry_on_failure`, which is why we hit this.)

2. **Even with `retry_on_failure` enabled, context-cancellation-driven
   shutdown defeats the carve-out.** In the same select in
   `retry_sender.go`, the `<-ctx.Done()` branch (immediately above the
   `<-rs.stopCh` branch) returns a plain wrapped error ("request is cancelled
   or timed out"), not a shutdown error — so a shutdown that propagates
   context cancellation into in-flight sends also results in deletion rather
   than retention. A request failing inside the exporter's push (before any
   backoff wait) during shutdown likewise never gets wrapped.

The net effect: the persistent queue's restart-durability guarantee holds for
items *at rest* in the queue, but items are silently lost if shutdown
coincides with destination unavailability — with the loss magnitude equal to
whatever the drain manages to dequeue and fail (potentially the whole queue).

**Steps to reproduce**
<!-- If possible, provide a recipe for reproducing the error. -->

Deterministic reproduction with any exporter that does not use
`retry_on_failure` (observed with the elasticsearch exporter; a testbed-based
reproduction exists in
`exporter/elasticsearchexporter/integrationtest` in contrib):

1. Configure an exporter with `sending_queue::storage: file_storage`.
2. Make the destination return errors (e.g. HTTP 503) so the queue starts
   accumulating.
3. Shut the collector down (or restart it) while the destination is still
   failing.
4. Restart with the same storage directory and restore the destination.

**What did you expect to see?**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you expected to see. -->

The backlog persisted during the outage is redelivered after
restart (per the `onDone` carve-out's stated intent).

**What did you see instead?**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you saw instead. -->

The shutdown-time drain completes each queued request with an
ordinary error; `onDone` deletes each from storage; the backlog is lost. In
our reproduction (~100 items/s load, 2s outage before restart), all items
enqueued during the outage window were missing at the backend and the count
never converged.

Note: a hard kill (no drain, no `onDone`) actually *preserves* the items via
`retrieveAndEnqueueNotDispatchedReqs` on restart — a clean shutdown loses
data that a crash would have kept.


### Collector version

v0.157.x

### Tip

<sub>[React](https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) with 👍 to help prioritize this issue. Please use comments to provide useful context, avoiding `+1` or `me too`, to help us triage it. Learn more [here](https://opentelemetry.io/community/end-user/issue-participation/).</sub>

items.title: missing data with persistent queues enabled during network outages
items.body: ### Component(s) extension/file_storage/storage ### What happened? **Describe the bug** Observed a consistency issue in gateway-collector when the otlphttp exporter queue uses file_storage for persistent queue storage. When **gateway-collector egress** is blocked with a network policy, **gateway-collector** experiences a network outage for approximately **3 days and 16 hours**. During recovery the data missing from the **first 4 hours** of the outage window. This has been reproduced multiple times with different window outages, and the missing data always appears at the beginning of the network connectivity issue. **Steps to reproduce** 1. Configure **gateway-collector** with persistent queue storage using `sending_queue.storage: file_storage/telemetry-retention`. 2. Apply a network policy that blocks **gateway-collector egress**. 3. Create a network outage 4. Restore connectivity. 5. Review the exported telemetry and compare the recovered data against the outage duration. **What did you expect to see?** All telemetry buffered during the outage should be retained and exported after connectivity is restored, including data from the start of the outage. **What did you see instead?** The **first 4 hours** of telemetry are consistently missing. The remaining telemetry for the rest of the outage period appears to be preserved. ### Collector version Contrib 0.127.0 ### Environment information ## Environment OS: (e.g., "Ubuntu 20.04") Compiler(if manually compiled): (e.g., "go 14.2") ### OpenTelemetry Collector configuration ```yaml otlphttp: endpoint: tls: insecure: false insecure_skip_verify: false sending_queue: block_on_overflow: true queue_size: 15000 storage: file_storage/telemetry-retention wait_for_result: true retry_on_failure: enabled: true initial_interval: 5s max_elapsed_time: 10m max_interval: 30s batch: send_batch_max_size: 1000 send_batch_size: 500 timeout: 10s extensions: file_storage/telemetry-retention: compaction: check_interval: 1m cleanup_on_start: true directory: on_rebound: true on_start: true create_directory: true directory: timeout: 10s service: extensions: - file_storage/telemetry-retention telemetry: logs: level: info pipelines: logs/pod: receivers: [otlp] processors: [memory_limiter, k8sattributes, batch] exporters: [otlphttp] ``` ### Log output ```shell ``` ### Additional context Am I missing something or my setup is incorrect? ### Tip [React](https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) with 👍 to help prioritize this issue. I'm in the process of evaluating the persistent queueing functionality. I'm using the v0.57.2 release. I am unable to get persistent queuing to work when using multiple replicas of the collector. I currently have two different environments I'm testing this out in and I cannot get either to work. Both of these environments are expected to handle a large volume of telemetry so we have autoscaling set up.

Our first environment is using K8s. We are using the [OpenTelemetry Helm chart](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-helm-charts/tree/main/charts/opentelemetry-collector) and have autoscaling enabled. I created a PVC with the `ReadWriteMany` access mode and mounted it using `extraVolumeMounts`. `persistent_storage_enabled` is set to `true` and the `directory` used by the `file_storage` extension matches the mounted volume path. items.title: [exporterhelper persistent-queue] Not working as expected
items.body:
### Component(s)

extension/storage/filestorage

### What happened?

## Description

I've been trying to use the storage extension and I'm having some trouble understanding it. The README is a bit confusing and the example is super basic.

When using the storage extension with `sending_queue.storage.file_storage` I can see that my traces, metrics and logs are being saved in the files `exporter_otlp_<signal>`, but that just happens when the data is exported.

Imagine the following scenario:

- Collector receives the data.
- The Batch processor is configured to wait for 30s to send the data.
- The Collector dies for some reason before exporting the data.

In that case, the data would be lost, and even when the Collector is restarted it wouldn't be aware of the missing data.

## Steps to Reproduce

I'll paste a simple app I'm using below, but this can be reproduced by using the Collector Config in here: https://github.com/julianocosta89/otel-lab/blob/main/q-and-a/otel-collector/otelcol-config.yaml

If you would like to test in the app, here it is:

```
git clone https://github.com/julianocosta89/otel-lab
cd otel-lab/q-and-a

docker compose up -d
```

After everything is up and running you can run the script `./requests.sh` to send 100 requests to the weather service.

Once the script is finished, you can kill the Collector and when starting it again nothing happens.

```
docker kill q-and-a-otel-collector-1

docker compose up -d
```

## Expected Result

I'd expect the received Traces, Metrics and Logs to be stored in the filesystem as soon as the Collector receives it, and if something happens before the data is exported, I'd expect the Collector to retry to send the data till it succeed.

I have this expectation due to this diagram here: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/tree/main/exporter/exporterhelper#persistent-queue

## Actual Result

If the Collector dies for some reason before exporting the data, the data is lost, and even when the Collector is restarted it isn't aware of the missing data.

### Collector version

Contrib 0.119.0

### Environment information

OS: MacOS Sequoia 15.3 (24D60)

But I'm running everything with Docker.


### OpenTelemetry Collector configuration

```yaml
extensions:
  file_storage: {}

receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:OTEL_COLLECTOR_HOST}:${env:OTEL_COLLECTOR_PORT_GRPC}
      http:
        endpoint: ${env:OTEL_COLLECTOR_HOST}:${env:OTEL_COLLECTOR_PORT_HTTP}
  postgresql:
    endpoint: ${env:POSTGRES_HOST}:${env:POSTGRES_PORT}
    username: ${env:POSTGRES_USER}
    password: ${env:POSTGRES_PWD}
    databases:
      - ${env:POSTGRES_DB}
    tls:
      insecure: true

processors:
  batch:
    timeout: 30s
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    metric_statements:
      - context: scope
        conditions:
          - name == "github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/receiver/postgresqlreceiver"
        statements:
          - set(resource.attributes["service.name"], "${env:POSTGRES_DB}")

connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}

exporters:
  debug: {}
  otlp:
    endpoint: "aspire-dashboard:18889"
    tls:
      insecure: true
    sending_queue:
      storage: file_storage
  otlp/jaeger:
    endpoint: "jaeger:4317"
    tls:
      insecure: true
    sending_queue:
      storage: file_storage

  extensions: [file_storage]
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
```

### Additional context

It would be great if we could have a more detailed documentation on how to use the components. In the main docs (opentelemetry.io) we only mention what are extensions, but there is not a single example there.
In the READMEs we have examples, but without data being actually sent anywhere, or even worse, with `nop` components.

items.title: OTELCollector continues export data although service is down
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

Hi, we've experienced weird behavior with the OTEL collector. We have a single application that reports a asynchronous `runtime.uptime` counter with cumulative temporality. Our dashboard shows the most recent (last one minute) applications that send this metric. For sure, only a single application is running, but we see two. After some investigation, we found out that the OTEL collector still sends data (based on the export interval), which makes that specific instance look like it is up. It feels like that a new metric stream continues the old one. We can eliminate a miss-configuration on the application side because **after a restart of the collectors, the export stopped and the application dissapeared from our dashboard**. Additionally, both metric streams have unique resource attributes. We can't reproduce it all the time.

**What version did you use?**
- OTELCollector: **0.93.0**
- Instrumentation client: v1.23.1 https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-contrib
- Exporter: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/exporter/clickhouseexporter

**What config did you use?**

items.title: Persistent queue can have data loss if last send was in error state before restarting/shutdown
items.body:
**Describe the bug**
Recently, a [new fix](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/6692) was added to prevent duplicate data by allowing writing to storage during shutdown. However, this has caused a side effect of data loss if the last send in the queue was in an error state. As `OnProcessingFinished` is always executed and the item is always removed from dispatched list even if the send was an error.

Examples of shutdown that can cause the problem:
- shut down would cause queue to stop looping processing of the item: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/exporter/exporterhelper/queued_retry.go#L438
- the error will propagate to the callback function but ignored: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/exporter/exporterhelper/queued_retry.go#L205
- OnProcessingFinished will be triggered:
  - persistent queue callback function: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/exporter/exporterhelper/internal/persistent_storage.go#L272
  - execution will remove the item from `currentlyDispatchedItems`
- After restarting, the item won't be processed again since it was considered dispatched 

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Create a pipeline with an exporter that is always failing to export
2. send a log entry to the pipeline
3. restart the pipeline with a new settings with an exporter that is able to send data

**What did you expect to see?**
After step 3 restart, it is expected the log is sent to the destination

**What did you see instead?**
The item was not seen in the exporter destination again. 

**What version did you use?**
Version: v0.67.0

**What config did you use?**
N/A

**Environment**
OS: mac
Compiler(if manually compiled): go 1.18

**Additional context**
A suggestion to fix the problem:
- Update `OnProcessingFinished` parameter to contain `error`
- pass in error from `consumerSender.send` to `OnProcessingFinished`
- Update persistent queue to not update storage if error is returned.

```
	qrs.queue.StartConsumers(qrs.cfg.NumConsumers, func(item internal.Request) {
		err := qrs.consumerSender.send(item)
		item.OnProcessingFinished(err)
	})
```

items.title: reenqueue may not be needed
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When I used the persistent queue, I found that the strategy dealing with requests that retry failed is different. The persistent queue enqueues these requests but the memory queue does not. In fact, users can configure the retry time themselves, if timeout, the request can be discarded intuitively. If reenqueue, the time a request tries to send is hard to know. So why not keep it simple and Let the user decide how long a request can be retried at most?

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We can remove the reenqueue feature to make it simple and intuitive so users can decide the retry time with the configuration.

items.title: Persistent queue should stop consumer before stopping producer
items.body:
**Describe the bug**
For exporters that use persistent queue, it is possible to send duplicate data when the exporter restarts(settings update) while sending data. This happens due to how persistent queue handles `Stop()` operation by shutting down `persistentStorage` first, which shuts down the underneath storage client. While the consumers are still processing, the success of process can't be updated to the storage client due to storage client being already closed.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Start a pipeline with the exporter having persistent queue enabled. The persistent queue uses a file storage extension.
2. Continuously send a lot of data through the pipeline
3. Update settings and trigger the pipeline to restart
4. check the exporting destination to verify events count

**What did you expect to see?**
At step 4, there should not be duplicate event

**What did you see instead?**
At step 4, there are duplicate events that are equal to # of consumers * batch of items. Since these batches of items were dispatched successfully but wasn't updated in the persistent queue storage.

**What version did you use?**
Version: v0.63.0

**What config did you use?**
Config: standard pipeline with exporter that enables persistent queue

**Environment**
OS: mac
Compiler(if manually compiled): go 1.18

**Additional context**
Code stack trace during close.
1. persistentQueue first close persistentStorage then the consumers: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/exporter/exporterhelper/internal/persistent_queue.go#L83
2. persistentStorage closes the underneath client before consumers are closed down(hence consumers can finish but fail to use storage client to update): https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/exporter/exporterhelper/internal/persistent_storage.go#L207

items.title: Persistent Queue Doesn't load di items after otel collector restarts
items.body:
**Describe the bug**
When exporter spawns up, the persistent queue(if enabled) should load persisted items during initialization. However, this behavior is not observed in 0.59.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Enable persistent queue with file_storage extension
2. Write a log data through the queue, set exporter destination to always fail
3. Observe item fail to be exported and item is present in the persisted file
4. update otel collector settings
5. wait for otel collector to restart

**What did you expect to see?**
Expected persistent queue to load currently dispatched item and attempt to dispatch

**What did you see instead?**
No item is loaded.

**What version did you use?**
Version: 0.59.0

**What config did you use?**
Exporter enable persistent queue
Enable file storage extension:
```
extension:
  file_storage:
    directory: "/tmp"
    timeout: "5s"
```

**Environment**
OS: mac Monterey

**Additional context**
I did some debugging locally and observe a couple things:
- I wrote a unit test in file_storage to write an item, then close the client and create a new client to attempt to read it. The unit test confirms the client is behaving correctly.
- I run my otel collector and then use bbolt cli to read the file. I can confirm all keys(di, ro, wi) required for persistent queue are present. However there isn't any data when I try to retrieve them(which can cause persistent queue to find no item to dispatch as it relies on values from di).

```
~/Desktop/repo/acies persistent-queue-poc ❯ bbolt keys /tmp/exporter_S2S_default_logs default                                                                                                                             09:18:06
di
ri
wi
~/Desktop/repo/acies persistent-queue-poc ❯ bbolt get /tmp/exporter_S2S_default_logs default ri                                                                                                                           09:18:07

~/Desktop/repo/acies persistent-queue-poc ❯ bbolt get /tmp/exporter_S2S_default_logs default wi                                                                                                                           09:18:32

~/Desktop/repo/acies persistent-queue-poc ❯ bbolt get /tmp/exporter_S2S_default_logs default di                                                                                                                           09:18:35
```

items.title: Persistent Queue Storage Should close client on stop
items.body:
**Describe the bug**
Persistent Queue(`persistentContiguousStorage`) retrieves a client from file storage and uses it to persist items. The current file storage uses a bbolt library, which locks the file it loads. This file stays locked until the fileStorageClient `Close` method is called.

However, when `persistentContiguousStorage` is [stopped](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/exporter/exporterhelper/internal/persistent_storage.go#L203), the client is not closed and the file underneath would stay locked. This would cause collector fail to restart when settings are updated due to file being locked.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Enable persistent queue and use file_storage extension as the storage client.
2. Run collector
3. Update settings
4. collector attempts to restart. Persistent queue fails to initialize and timeout from file_lock.

**What did you expect to see?**
At step 4, the collector should start successfully

**What did you see instead?**
file has been locked. client is unable to open file

**What version did you use?**
Version: 0.58.0

**Environment**
OS: Mac Monterey
Compiler(if manually compiled): Go 1.17

**Additional context**
Suggestion to fix: when `persistentContiguousStorage` `stop` is [called](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/exporter/exporterhelper/internal/persistent_storage.go#L203). Call `pcs.client.Close(context.Background())`.

Edited the file locally and verify the collector can start successfully

items.title: Improving resiliency through disk buffering capability
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Currently, collector buffers all data in memory, which can lead to data loss in case buffer gets overfilled (e.g. during temporary exporter connection issues) or due to a sudden crash. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**

There should be a possibility to enable disk buffering capability. For example, exporter could buffer the incoming data on disk (up to the defined limit) and clear the buffer as data gets sent out. In case of restart, recovery process could happen, which would send-out the buffered data.

Perhaps this capability could be a good fit to `queued_retry` [helper](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/master/exporter/exporterhelper/queued_retry.go), since it already manages send queues?

**Additional context**
[Gitter discussion](https://gitter.im/open-telemetry/community?at=5fd326c53dd3b251a4fc4629)

items.title: Log Collection Proof of Concept: Validate Chained Approach

milestone.title: Backlog
milestone.description: Issues are assigned to the backlog when the target release milestone is unknown.

items.body:
We want to validate that chaining FluentBit and OpenTelemetry Collector
is a viable approach to support collection of logs in formats that FluentBit
supports and which we would like to avoid implementing directly in Collector.

Chained approach implies that FluentBit collects logs from file logs (and
possibly from other sources), sends them to the Collector, then Collector sends
the logs to the backend.

We will use [Fluentd Forward Protocol v1](https://github.com/fluent/fluentd/wiki/Forward-Protocol-Specification-v1) to send logs from FluentBit to Collector. 
We will use OTLP to send logs from Collector to the backend.

The primary concerns that need to be clarified are:

- What is the performance impact of chained approach? How much more CPU and RAM
  is used by Collector when logs are passed through it compared to the scenario
  when the same logs are collected by FluentBit and send to the backend?

- How much latency (delay in log delivery) is added by Collector?

- What is the impact of Collector crashing? How much logs are queued in memory
  and will be lost? Is queuing necessary of can be minimized/avoided to minimize
  the losses? Can we run with 0-sized queue in Collector and rely on queuing and
  batching done by FluentBit?
  
- If queuing is necessary what is the impact of adding persistent queues that
  survive the crash and restart of Collector?

In order to clarify these concerns the following tasks need to be performed:

- [x] [Add logs as a supported data type to Collector.](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/957)
- [x] [Implement Fluentd Forward Protocol v1 receiver in Collector.](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/1016)
- [x] [Add LogService definition to experimental `logsproto`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/1052)
- [x] [Implement `logsproto` logs exporter in Collector (add to `otlpexporter`).](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/1053)
- [x] Define interesting scenarios to test performance.
- [x] Decide if we want to run performance tests manually or adapt Collector
  testbed to automate it.
- [x] Run test scenarios and measure resource consumption by FluentBit+Collector
  chained. 
- [x] Record and publish test results, findings, recommendations.

Note: `logsproto` is the experimental version of OTLP Logs Protocol. Receiver and exporter for this protocol will be added to existing `otlp` receiver and exporter, but the implementation is experimental and subject to change, so we will not document for end users how it is configured and enabled (developer documentation is still necessary).
